text:
maria: Heads-up — noticed dashboard tail numbers look wrong for /v1/generate after the quota tweak this morning. p99 jumped from ~420ms to ~950ms but raw logs don't show a backend spike.
jake: I saw that too. Did routing shift any traffic to the warm pool variant? the rollout note said 'prefer-low-latency' but didn't mention sample attribution changes.
alex: Deploy bot shows the policy change at 1760019600: `policy:update prefer-low-latency -> weight 0.6` :deploy-bot:  
deploy-bot: policy:update completed by @ops at 2025-06-12T14:00:00Z
sophia: Quick question: are percentiles in the console computed per-endpoint aggregate (merge of route slices) or per-route then merged? That would explain a p99 jump if we merged uneven sample sizes.
maria: I think console uses a rollup that combines tdigest shards from each route without reweighting by client sample count — so heavier-weighted fast routes can mask the mid-tail, then a fallback route with fewer samples but higher latencies can dominate p99 when weights change.
jake: That matches my local reproduction. Ran this on a small dump: `SELECT approx_percentile(latency_ms, 0.99) FROM traces WHERE endpoint = '/v1/generate' GROUP BY route_tag` then naive merge produced different result than `SELECT approx_percentile(latency_ms, 0.99) FROM traces WHERE endpoint = '/v1/generate'` combined across routes.
alex: Can you paste the reproduction steps? I can check the console merge code.
sophia: Repro steps I used:
```
-- per-route
SELECT route_tag, percentile_cont(0.99) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY latency_ms) as p99
FROM sample_traces
WHERE endpoint='/v1/generate'
GROUP BY route_tag;
-- global
SELECT percentile_cont(0.99) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY latency_ms) as p99
FROM sample_traces
WHERE endpoint='/v1/generate';
```
Result: per-route p99s = [routeA: 450, routeB: 1800] global combined p99 = 520 (but console shows ~950). Means console merge logic isn't doing a strict merge of raw samples.
maria: Console uses tdigest rollups at ingestion which loses some fidelity depending on bucket counts. Also routing weight changes can change which tdigest dominates the merged digest.
jake: So the quota/routing tweak increased routeB's relative contribution to the endpoint and since routeB's tdigest was sparse it inflated merged p99? Sounds plausible.
sophia: Two quick mitigation ideas:
• show both "merged percentile" and "per-route p99s" side-by-side in the latency pane
• add a badge that explains the sample source (route weights + digest merge) — hover -> short explanation
alex: Agreed. UX idea: add a little legend item "percentile provenance" that toggles to show origin breakdown (route counts, tdigest samples, raw-sample fallback). Could be a small dot next to p99.
maria: Short-term fix: add an endpoint debug view that surfaces raw sample counts per route and a link to run the exact SQL that computes the global percentile from raw rows (for audits).
jake: I'll open a PR to (1) surface per-route p50/p95/p99 in the default split view and (2) add a tooltip line about aggregation method. PR will include a test that compares digest-merge result vs raw-sample percentile on synthetic data.
alex: Can you also include a small e2e check that flags big delta between merged-tdigest and raw percentile (>15%) and surfaces as a warning on the dashboard? We had a customer confusion once and that would prevent surprise.
sophia: Good call. I'll add a quick alert rule draft.
maria: For action items:
• @jake open PR with UI + tooltip + tests
• @alex add backend endpoint to expose per-route raw counts and run-audit SQL
• @sophia draft alert rule and short doc blurb explaining when to trust merged percentiles
• I'll follow up with a short note to support explaining why p99 could diverge after routing changes
jake: PR opened: https://git.company/repo/pull/4821 — includes screenshots and test harness. Please review.
alex: Reviewing now. If all looks good we can roll the UI change behind a flag and ship today.
sophia: minor nit — wording on tooltip should avoid 'tdigest' for non-technical readers. Use 'sampled merge' + 'may differ from raw-row percentile'.
maria: Yep. Thanks everyone. Filing a tiny postmortem note after we deploy so CSM has a clear explanation for customers who ping about p99 weirdness.
